column7: #2846 review finding, live on main after #3023: on the passwordless path the user handle is attacker-chosen, and a handle above MaxInt64 makes Postgres's driver fail to encode the id (an error that is not ErrUserNotFound), so the request was classed as a pre-verdict storage error: audited auth.login_error and its per-IP slot handed back -- unlimited unthrottled requests, each spoofing an outage in the audit trail. Observed against real Postgres (store.GetUser(MaxInt64+1) returns "failed to encode args[0] ... greater than maximum value for int64"); SQLite turns the same id into not-found. Fixed in core: a handle decoding to 0 or above MaxInt64 is refused as malformed before any lookup. The test reproduces the Postgres driver answer over the SQLite fixture and asserts webauthn.failed, no auth.login_error, slot kept, the response byte-identical to a handle naming no user, and that no out-of-range id reaches storage. Red by mutation (guard disabled): both out-of-range cases fail on all four assertions.
